Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc-Lko:30141
Court No. - 12
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 4099 of 2024

Applicant :- Ram Dular Alias Sonu Yadav
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Its Prin. Secy. Home, Lucknow And 3 Others

Counsel for Applicant :- Dinesh Chandra Tewari
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and Mohd. Taiyab, who has filed Vakalatnama on behalf of the informant and perused the record.
The Vakalatnama is taken on record.

2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.510 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 323,
506, 372, 376 DA of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act, Police Station Chinhat, District Lucknow.
3. In terms of the FIR, it was alleged that the daughter of the informant aged about 15 years went missing on 20.11.2023, none was named in the FIR.

Subsequently, in the statement under Section Ram Dular Alias Sonu Yadav vs State Of U.P. Thru. Its Prin. Secy. Home, ... on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38427919/
1 161 of Cr.P.C., the victim stated that there was one Badal, who used to stayed in the neighbourhood and was friendly to the victim, used to visit home.

entities.text: Section Ram Dular Alias Sonu Yadav vs State Of U.P. Thru. Its Prin. Secy. Home
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: The victim further stated that she used to go to a salon to acquire the skills.

She also stated that on 20.11.2023, when she had gone from home to visit the salon, she met the mother of the said Badal, who took her for roaming and had promised her to leave her back and on the said promise, she sat in the car.
It was also alleged that she forced and persuaded her to marry her son and also stated that she will ensure that the victim get a good job.
The victim specifically stated that nothing wrong was done to her by any one.

Subsequently, in the statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., she drastically changed the version by saying that on the said date, she was met with the applicant as well as the mother of the friend Badal, who took her in car for Charbagh, where, they had taken lunch in a hotel and thereafter the applicant snatched her phone and took her to a home, where, she stayed for five days and wrong was also committed by the applicant.
She specifically stated that the mother of her was friend throughout, present in the room.
She also stated that she was administered some medicine and she used to force to work as a sex worker.
She also made wild allegation that the said two persons took money and started sending her to have sex with various persons.
She also stated that the accused want to merry her to Badal.
She also made allegations against one Anamika Kumari.

She also stated that the medical was not done and ultimately on 31.12.2023, when the accused wanted to take her to Hyderabad on a fake ID, she escaped from there.
4.
The Counsel for the applicant argues that the medical report on record does not corroborate any of the allegations with regard to the offence under Section 376 of IPC.
There is no material to demonstrate the presence of the victim from 20.11.2023 to 31.12.2023 on record.
There is no definite document as prescribed under Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice Act to form any view with regard to the age of the victim at this stage.
5. The Counsel for the informant strongly opposes the bail application by firstly arguing that in the affidavit, the relationship of the deponent with the applicant has not been disclosed.

He places reliance on the order dated 10.04.20219 passed in Bail No.3690 of 2019 (Dharmendra Singh vs State of U.P.), wherein, the Court had directed the Senior Registrar to ensure that without disclosing the relation between the deponent and the applicant in the affidavit, the bail application should not be accepted.

entities.text: Bail No.3690 of 2019 (Dharmendra Singh vs State of U.P.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further argues that the same deponent has filed bail applications on behalf of the other three co-accused persons, thus, on that count alone, the bail application should be rejected.
6. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

7. Considering the said submissions, it is essential to notice the provisions as contained in the Allahabad High Court Rules with regard to the filing of the bail application, which are in Chapter XVIII Rule18 and sub-section (8) of Rule 18-A, which are to the following effect:
"18. Application for bail other than the anticipatory bail:- (1) No application for bail shall be entertained unless accompanied by a copy of judgment or order appealed against or sought to be revised and a copy of order passed by the Sessions Judge on the bail application for the applicant and unless the accused has surrendered except where he has been release on bail after conviction under Section 389 (3) of the Code Ram Dular Alias Sonu Yadav vs State Of U.P. Thru. Its Prin. Secy. Home, ... on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38427919/
2 of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

entities.text: Code Ram Dular Alias Sonu Yadav vs State Of U.P. Thru. Its Prin. Secy. Home
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Explanation :- the copy of the order refusing bail passed by the Sessions Judge shall either be a certified copy or the copy furnished by the Sessions Judge free of charge to the accused.

(2) Every application for bail in a case which is under investigation or which is pending in a lower Court shall state whether application for bail had or had not been previously made before the Magistrate and the Sessions Judge concerned and the results of such applications, if any.
(3) Save in exceptional circumstances- (a) No bail application shall be placed before the Court unless notice thereof has been given to the Government Advocate and a period of two days has elapsed from the date of such notice.

(b) If the application for bail has not been moved within seven days after the expiry of the aforesaid period of two days the applicant or his counsel shall give two days previous notice to the Government Advocate as to the exact date on which such application is intended to be moved.

(c) Where the prayer for bail is contained in a petition of appeal or application for revision, notice thereof may be given to the Government Advocate the same day prior to the hearing of such petition or application and the fact of such previous notice having been given, shall be endorsed on such petition or application.
Alongwith such notice a certified copy or one attested to be true by the counsel, of the Judgment appealed from or sought to be revised shall also be given to the Government Advocate.]

(4) Every application for bail shall show prominently in the first page thereof the crime number, the police station by which and the section or sections and the Act or Rules under which the applicant is being prosecuted or has been convicted and whether such application is the first, second or any such subsequent application moved by him before this Court, and shall be accompanied by a copy of the first information report.

The Bench Secretary shall while entertaining a bail application for presentation to the court check every page there of and shall affix a rubber stamp containing his initials on every page of the bail application and all the annexures thereto before putting it up before the court in token of his having checked, every page of the applications and he shall, thereafter, make the following endorsement on the bail application :

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly the official whose duty it is to receive the bail application from the court after orders, shall affix a rubber stamp containing his initials on the first page of the bail application in token of his having checked that all the pages of the bail application bear the rubber stamp of the Bench Secretary.

The rubber stamps containing the initials of the Bench Secretary and the official or officials authorised to receive fresh bail application from the Court shall be supplied to the Bench Secretaries and the officials by the Registrar General of the Court.
The application shall not be returned to the applicant or his counsel after the above endorsement has been made.]
(5) Every page of the application for bail and every page of the annexures thereto shall bear the full signature of the applicant or his counsel.

(6) In every such application shall be stated the full particulars of the previous application or applications, if any, moved in this Court by same applicant in respect of the same crime and the date or dates on which such previous application or applications had been rejected.]
18-A Application for bail under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

(8) While presenting an application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 before the High Court, the requirement of filing affidavit as per sub-rule (2) shall be subject to the provisions applicable for filing bail applications under Rul 18.

The said rule shall, as far as practicable, be applicable for the applications under Section 438, Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973]"
8.

On a plain reading of the abovesaid two rules, the submission of the Counsel for the informant merits rejection as in the present application, the deponent has specifically stated that she is the aunt of the applicant.

9. Considering the arguments raised at the bar, prima facie, in the FIR and in the statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C., there is no allegation against the applicant, in fact, even the applicant was not named in the statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. and subsequently, in the statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.

, scandalous allegations have been levelled against various persons including the applicant, which on the face of it highly improbable; there is no material to infer, at this stage,
about the presence of the victim from 20.11.2023 upto 31.12.2023; there is no medical on record to corroborate the allegations, thus, on all these grounds, a prima facie view can be formed that the statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. is not relevant.

10. Considering all these facts and grounds coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal antecedents and is languishing in jail since 02.01.2024, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.
